newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Bossi begins his "March to the Sea".
newsitem.headline: Italy's Bossi begins his "March to the Sea".

text.p: Separatist leader Umberto Bossi launched a weekend of demonstrations along Italy's River Po on Friday that will lead to a planned proclamation of "independence" on Sunday for his self-styled northern republic.

The Northern League party leader filled a Venetian glass flask with water at this mountain source of Italy's longest river to begin a three-day "March to the Sea" which he hopes will draw at least one million followers of his breakaway plan.

The weekend of demonstrations, expected to meet counter-rallies by supporters of Italian unity, is due to end on Sunday with Bossi's proclamation in Venice of a "federal republic of Padania", the name he gives his self-styled state.

The firebrand separatist has said he hopes the symbolic proclamation will be followed within a year by full independence for a region encompassing the richest areas of Italy and its industrial heartland.

Bossi has brushed off evidence that his separatist push has little support, even among the League's own voters. One opinion poll published on Friday showed only 7.6 percent of Italians were in favour of splitting the nation.

Bossi's campaign has been condemned across the political spectrum. All his opponents say federal reform is the best response to popular frustration with high taxes, government bureaucracy and public sector inefficiency.
